sources.citation: Gatschet, Albert S. 1891. The Karankawa Indians, the coast people of Texas. Archaeological and Ethnological Papers of the Peabody Museum 1(2). Cambridge, MA: Peabody Museum. (Bidai: p. 39 and footnote 2, printing Rufus Grimes's letter of 15 Nov 1887)
sources.note: Nothing. This footnote IS the entire Bidai corpus: numerals 1-6 (namah, nahonde, naheestah, nashirimah, nahot nahonde, nashees nahonde) plus púskus 'boy' and tándshai 'maize', written from memory by a settler; Gatschet only remarks that the numerals all begin in na- and infers (wrongly, per later authors) a Caddo affiliation. Two acute accent marks are printed, no statement.
sources.venue: Archaeological and Ethnological Papers of the Peabody Museum
